Order 
This first application has been filed by applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.157/2023 registered at Police Station Karera Gulabganj, District Vidisha (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376,
376(2)(n), 305 of IPC and Section 5L/6 of POCSO Act.
Applicant is in judicial custody since 14.12.2023

As per the case of prosecution, brother of victim reported to Police Station Gulabganj,
District Vidisha that his sister aged around 15 years and 5 months is missing since intervening night of 12.09.2023 and 13.09.2023.
Some unknown person has enticed and taken his daughter.
Police Station Gulabganj registered FIR at Crime No.157/2023 for offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC.
During investigation, Police Station Santej, District Gandhinagar, Gujarat informed that the dead body of victim was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:13658 2 MCRC-34365-2024 found on railway track.
Her dead body was forwarded for post-mortem examination.
The Medical Officer suspected her pregnant with eight months.
It was further informed that Kamal Adiwasi had kept the victim as his wife.

Kamal used to harass and manhandle her for labour work, therefore,
victim has committed suicide by train.
On such allegations, prosecution for offence punishable under Sections 366, 376, 376 (2)(n), 305 of IPC and Section 5L/6 of POCSO Act was added.
Kamal @ Rahul was arrested on 13.12.2023.
He is in custody ever since.

On completion of investigation,
final report was submitted on 02.02.2024.
The trial is underway.

sentences.text: Learned Counsel for the applicant in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in the matter.
No offence as alleged is committed by the applicant.
Learned counsel referring to the evidence of Hanlubhai Patel (PW- 3) submits that the only witness with regard to co-habitation of victim with the accused has been examined.
The other five material witnesses have also been examined, therefore, there is no likelihood of tampering with remaining evidence by applicant.
Learned counsel referring to the DNA report dated 31.05.2024 submits that DNA report clearly exonerates the applicant.
Learned counsel further submits that applicant is aged around 24 years and is Labourer by profession.
He is sole bread earner of the family, therefore, there is no likelihood of absconsion leaving his family and home.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
No further custodial interrogation is required in the matter.
The trial would take time to complete.
Jail incarceration is causing hardship to the applicant.
Therefore, applicant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:13658 3 MCRC-34365-2024 may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
